messages:
alina: Heads up — seeing ~8 nodes in us-west2-gpu-pool flip to NotReady/NoSchedule since 03:24UTC. Pods requesting nvidia.com/gpu are Pending and cluster-autoscaler is thrashing because nodes come up but become Unschedulable quickly.

sam: Can you paste node status and kubelet/driver logs? pinging @eng-infra for visibility.

alina: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gw-usw2-gpu` shows several entries:
gw-usw2-gpu-01   NotReady,NoSchedule   0/1   10.4.1.23
gw-usw2-gpu-02   NotReady,NoSchedule   0/1   10.4.1.24
...

alina: kubelet logs (tail):
```
Apr 15 03:23:59 kubelet[1234]: E0415 03:23:59.12345 kubelet.go:242] Failed to start device plugin manager: failed to create plugin watcher: watch /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/: no such file or directory
Apr 15 03:24:01 nvidia-driver-installer[1]: ERROR: modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.19.0-xx
Apr 15 03:24:02 nvidia-device-plugin[1]: ERROR: failed to register with kubelet: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: TLS handshake error"
```

mike: Looks like the driver module never built/loaded, so nvidia-smi will fail and the device plugin exits. The TLS handshake line worries me — is kubelet restarting during installer run?

alina: `nvidia-smi` hangs on affected nodes, `lsmod | grep nvidia` returns nothing. Driver installer daemonset is CrashLoopBackOff. Driver pod logs end with: `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.19.0-xx` then the installer attempts a kubelet restart which triggers short TLS errors in device-plugin registration.

irene: We've seen this pattern when host kernel headers don't match the running kernel or when a host OS upgrade happened and the driver build failed silently. Can you check `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)` and if headers are installed?

alina: Confirmed: kernel headers missing on nodes that were provisioned in the 03:00 window. There was a host OS image update pushed last night that may have changed the kernel flavor.

vlad: Quick mitigations: cordon and drain noncritical workloads from the affected nodes, then either reboot or reinstall headers+driver. I can cordon 6 nodes now.

ops-oncall: I've cordoned 6 nodes and started a rolling reboot on the other 3. Cluster-autoscaler still attempts scale-up but new nodes hit NotReady. Putting a hold on CA for the gpu nodegroup now.

sam: Proposed plan: 1) Pause autoscaler for gpu pool to avoid churn. 2) Patch the driver-installer image to check kernel headers and fail safely (no kubelet restart) 3) Deploy canary with fixed installer image to a small canary nodepool.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: daemonset/nvidia-driver-installer -> image redwood-infra/nvidia-driver-installer:1.2.1 -> target nodepool us-west2-gpu-canary

mike: :thumbsup: Also consider reverting the OS image update if we confirm it introduced the header mismatch. Will open a PR to revert the image in our builder.

alina: Cost/impact note: The capacity shortage forced ~40 inference jobs onto CPU-only nodes (higher SLO latency and increased cost due to fallback autoscaling). We should track the cost delta and customer-facing SLA impact.

irene: Escalating to infra-ml + platform-release. I'll collect full driver build logs and attach to the incident ticket.

kube-bot: Alert: cluster-autoscaler suppressed scale-ups for group us-west2-gpu due to repeated node notReady events within 10m window.

ops-oncall: Will update incident channel with progress. Uncordon nodes as they pass `nvidia-smi` and `kubectl get nodes` shows Ready.

alina: Thanks all — canary is our priority. Will post results from the first 2 nodes once the new installer finishes.
